baseline_models.focus_anchor: The coordinated dative nouns in 70:25 name an asker at word 1 and a deprived person at word 2.
baseline_models.mechanism: The pair establishes two access channels to the same allocation: need made legible by a request and need legible only through deprivation. Coordination prevents silence from becoming disqualification.

activation_trace.role: Asking and requesting supplies the voiced channel by which a need becomes socially legible.
Deprivation and failure to obtain what was sought supplies the silent-status channel that does not depend on a spoken request.

changed_reading.before: The verse lists two roughly synonymous kinds of poor recipient.
changed_reading.after: The verse closes a visibility gap: allocation must reach both the person who can ask and the person whose deprivation never becomes a request.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The lām governing both recipient nouns directs performance toward them, while the deprived noun carries a branch of protected right as well as lack.
baseline_models.mechanism: Fulfilling a request and preserving an inviolable claim converge on discharge rather than discretionary generosity. The recipient is modeled as already holding a claim that the possessor must recognize.

activation_trace.role: The literal fulfillment of a request makes transfer the completion of an outstanding matter rather than a new favor.
The inviolable claim, pact, and right image gives the deprived recipient protected standing within the allocation mechanism.

changed_reading.before: A possessor elects to confer aid on two needy classes.
changed_reading.after: A possessor discharges a recipient-held claim, whether that claim is voiced by asking or remains protected despite silence.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah first presents an asking act in an ominous request, so asking cannot itself certify virtue. Repetition at 70:25 instead makes the request a legibility signal to which the allocation rule responds without requiring the requester to be sentimentalized.

activation_trace.role: The doubled image of asking and requesting supplies a morally unsettled instance of the same communicative act later naming a recipient.
The focus asker anchors the revision: a request opens access to the fixed allocation without functioning as a certificate of moral worth.

structural_cues: The same root opens the surah in a doubled construction at 70:1 and returns as the first recipient noun at 70:25.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: the same asking root occurs in an ominous opening request and in the focus recipient; inference: the rule responds to asking as an access signal rather than a merit test; live alternative: the repetition may only contrast two unrelated objects of request.

changed_reading.before: The asker is presumed to be a morally exemplary needy person.
changed_reading.after: The asker's speech makes a claim actionable, while the allocation disciplines the holder of wealth rather than inviting a worthiness screen.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later recipient rule answers an earlier scene in which even intimate-to-intimate asking has collapsed. A standing channel for asker and deprived therefore works before crisis and beyond kin reciprocity, when personal closeness can no longer carry aid.

activation_trace.role: Reciprocal questioning supplies the social exchange that fails in the crisis scene and must be preempted by a standing distributive practice.
Intimate kinship supplies the strongest reciprocal bond, whose failure shows why access cannot depend on personal closeness.
The focus request becomes the ordinary-world signal served by an institution not restricted to intimates.
Deprivation supplies the nonreciprocal condition that remains eligible even when no intimate speaks for it.

structural_cues: At 70:10 the negated asking relation is explicitly between two intimates; 70:25 names recipients without a kin qualifier.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: intimate asking disappears in the crisis scene and the focus later names asker and deprived; inference: the fixed channel rehearses aid before relational collapse and outside kin reciprocity; live alternative: 70:10 may describe only eschatological isolation, not the design of ordinary distribution.

changed_reading.before: Aid is a personal response within familiar reciprocal relationships.
changed_reading.after: The recipient pair defines a preemptive, nonkin channel that remains intelligible when intimacy and reciprocal asking fail.

context_deltas.mechanism: Gathering converts dispersed goods into a mass, containment closes that mass, and the withheld hand blocks giftable good from leaving it. The deprived recipient can therefore be read not only as an existing category but as the social result of accumulation plus blocked outflow.

activation_trace.role: Gathering dispersed things into one mass supplies the concentration stage of the deprivation-producing mechanism.
Enclosing something in a vessel supplies the storage boundary that stops concentrated goods from circulating.
Good as generosity and gift identifies the stored material as something capable of outward transfer.
The literal hand withheld from giving supplies the final blockade that turns possession into another person's deprivation.
Deprivation and missed provision names the human endpoint produced when giftable good remains gathered and enclosed.

structural_cues: The sequence moves from gathering and enclosing at 70:18, through withholding good at 70:21, to the exception whose wealth opens toward named recipients at 70:24-25.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: gathering, enclosure, giftable good, withholding, and deprivation occur in sequence; inference: blocked circulation helps cause or maintain the deprived condition; live alternative: the context may juxtapose a possessor's vice and a recipient category without asserting direct causation.

changed_reading.before: The deprived person is a static needy type encountered by an otherwise independent giver.
changed_reading.after: The deprived person can be an effect of the holder's gathering, enclosing, and withholding, so allocation repairs a deprivation the ownership pattern may itself produce.

context_deltas.mechanism: Continuance turns distribution into a stable practice; wealth supplies the held stock; an owner-specific obligatory right places a liability inside that stock; and a distinguishing mark makes the liability identifiable. The focus pair names the destinations of that durable allocation.

activation_trace.role: Stillness and continuance supplies the temporal stability carried from sustained practice into the adjacent wealth obligation.
Acquiring and accumulating wealth supplies the held stock within which the recipient liability resides.
A specific right owned by its holder supplies the legal architecture that precedes and governs the focus recipients.
A distinguishing mark that guides to a thing makes the allocated liability identifiable rather than improvised at the moment of asking.
Fulfilling a request makes the asker one destination at which the already marked liability is discharged.
The inviolable claim gives the silent recipient ownership-like standing in the same durable liability.

structural_cues: The incomplete recipient phrase at 70:25 directly completes the known right located in wealth at 70:24.
The focus pair is therefore syntactically downstream of a right, not merely of a general command to be generous.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: continuance, accumulated wealth, an owner-specific right, a distinguishing mark, and two dative recipients are adjacent; inference: they form a durable earmarked liability; live alternative: known may indicate a recognized amount or duty without implying formal bookkeeping.

changed_reading.before: Giving is an episodic response triggered when need becomes visible.
changed_reading.after: The asker and deprived are standing destination accounts for a durable, identifiable liability already embedded in one's wealth.

context_deltas.mechanism: The branch link between truth-making and a financial right, followed by the image of monetary debt, makes distribution an enacted verification of accountability. Paying the focus recipients materializes rather than merely accompanies affirmation of the coming account.

activation_trace.role: Alms as a financial right supplies the material act through which professed truth becomes economically verifiable.
Monetary debt supplies the liability model that connects the coming account to payment of the recipient-held share.
The recipient's inviolable claim is the focus liability whose discharge makes accountability concrete.

structural_cues: Affirming the day of account at 70:26 follows immediately after the wealth-right and recipient unit at 70:24-25.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: the adjacent roots supply financial right, debt, and the focus claim; inference: paying recipients enacts confidence in final accounting; live alternative: dīn here may activate judgment and recompense without making the human share a literal debt.

changed_reading.before: Giving is one ethical sign placed beside belief in judgment.
changed_reading.after: Giving is debt-like performance that verifies belief in an account by settling an accountable claim in the present.

context_deltas.mechanism: Guarding an inviolable boundary, preserving a warranty-bearing covenant, and actively monitoring a charge extend the focus claim into stewardship. The possessor holds wealth with another person's protected interest already inside it.

activation_trace.role: Protecting sanctity, covenant, and chastity supplies a guarded-boundary model for preserving another's inviolable interest.
A warranted undertaking secured against later liability supplies the accountable custody structure for the wealth share.
Watching and tending a matter supplies the active stewardship needed to keep the recipient's share from disappearing into possession.
The inviolable claim, pact, and right gives the deprived recipient the protected interest being guarded.

structural_cues: The wealth-right unit belongs to a repeated series of maintained practices that later includes guarded boundaries, covenants, testimony, and renewed prayer.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: guarding, warranty-bearing covenant, tending, and an inviolable focus claim appear in one practice series; inference: ownership is recast as custody of another's share; live alternative: these may remain parallel virtues rather than one stewardship mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The giver owns a surplus outright and chooses to alienate part of it.
changed_reading.after: The holder is a steward guarding a preexisting interest of the asker and deprived within the wealth under custody.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later exposure of ungrounded appetite limits a possible overreading of the asker. Asking makes need visible, but desire does not manufacture the right; the focus claim remains governed by the already known allocation.

activation_trace.role: The heart's covetous hope supplies the counterexample showing that wanting or expecting something is not itself an entitlement.
The sought request supplies the asker's desire, now constrained by the known-right frame rather than treated as self-validating.
The inviolable claim supplies the objective standing that distinguishes entitlement from mere appetite.

structural_cues: The focus recipients complete a known right, whereas 70:38 interrogates each person's expectation of entry into delight.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: the focus joins request to a known right, while the later root supplies covetous hope; inference: speech activates access but cannot create entitlement by itself; live alternative: the later appetite concerns eschatological entry and may not directly qualify material requests.

changed_reading.before: Any expressed want is enough to constitute the asker's right.
changed_reading.after: Asking makes a qualifying claim visible, but the claim is grounded in the known allocation rather than generated by appetite.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant split mapping from the focus root to S-L-L rather than the ordinary morphology of the asker. It remains anchored to focus word 1 and coheres with the silent recipient at word 2, but downstream prose must present it only as a material activation analogy, never as an etymology or alternate translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Focus word 1 carries a packet-authorized non-dominant mapped inventory whose water-channel image can model how a claim opens stored wealth toward word 2.

activation_trace.role: A narrow channel where water gathers and passes supplies an exploratory image of the asker as an outlet through which held wealth begins to flow.
Deprivation supplies the low-access condition reached by that channel even when no request supplies its own outlet.

changed_reading.before: The asker is only a vocal beneficiary standing outside the possessor's wealth.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the asker is a flow channel that draws an allocated share out of enclosure, while the deprived names need that lacks such a channel.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This convergence is surprising because the cited branches are distant from the local oath, emergence, and erected-target surfaces at 70:40 and 70:43. It remains valid as packet-supplied branch imagery anchored to the focus dative destinations and protected claim, but it must be rendered as a cross-domain model of allocation, not as a lexical gloss of those context words or proof of a quantified legal rule.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The lām pair in 70:25 gives an outward transfer two specified destinations, and the protected-claim branch of word 2 supplies the owner-like endpoint.

activation_trace.role: Separating and apportioning a share supplies the first operation: carving the recipient portion out of undivided holdings.
Money going out along a known direction supplies the second operation: moving the apportioned share toward specified recipients.
An assigned share raised for its owner supplies the marked endpoint that keeps outflow attached to a claimant rather than becoming diffuse generosity.
Fulfilling the request identifies one focus destination at which the apportioned outflow is completed.
The inviolable claim identifies the silent recipient as an owner-like endpoint even without a voiced request.

changed_reading.before: The focus names beneficiaries of an undifferentiated charitable outflow.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the focus completes a three-stage mechanism: apportion a share, send it along a known direction, and terminate it at the voiced or silent holder of the claim.

strongest_changes: The deprived person shifted from a static social type to a condition that gathering, enclosure, and withholding can produce or maintain.
The recipient pair shifted from optional beneficiaries to standing holders of a durable, identifiable liability embedded in wealth.
Asking shifted from a moral credential to an access signal: it makes a qualifying claim visible, while silence and lack of kin reciprocity do not erase the claim.
summary.what_was_special: The focus pair generated a voice-versus-silence axis, while the deprivation root also opened an inverse image of inviolable right. Context then supplied a causal blockage, an owner-specific known share, debt and accounting, and guarded covenant, allowing economic circulation and stewardship models to coexist without collapsing into one final interpretation.
remaining_uncertainties: The S-L-L flow-channel outlier depends on a non-dominant split mapping and must remain analogy rather than morphology.
Debt, destination-account, and stewardship language may describe a mechanism without establishing a formal legal equivalence.
The failed intimate asking at 70:10 and covetous hope at 70:38 may constrain the focus requester only by juxtaposition rather than direct semantic government.
